notes: PARENT-TOO-YOUNG RESOLVED for William Cheesman, and extended further (research 2026-07-04): William Cheesman (b.1728) is almost certainly NOT this Martha's son, and neither (on closer look) are Thomas (1734) or Mary Ann (1746). Peter Cheesman (I182195863485) had at least three wives before/besides Martha. WikiTree's independently cross-linked profiles (Cheesman-112 Peter, Cheesman-113 Thomas, Cheseman-5 Mary Ann Jackson, Ellis-4456 Ann Hanna Ellis) agree with each other -- and match this tree's own exact birth/death dates for Thomas and Mary Ann -- that Thomas (b. 11 May 1734) and Mary Ann (b. 16 Sep 1746) are children of Peter's second wife, **Ann Hanna Ellis** (b. 16 Apr 1710 England, d. 1759 Gloucester NJ; married Peter in 1732 per WikiTree, or 'c.1746' per the unpublished 'Cheesman Family' manuscript by Albert Stirling Adams, Gloucester Co. NJ Historical Society, transcribed at https://www.longislandsurnames.com/getperson.php?personID=I0675&tree=Roe). William (1728) predates either marriage date given for Ann Ellis, so he belongs to an even earlier, unidentified first wife of Peter's (the Adams manuscript itself asks, unresolved, 'who was the mother of his children'). A previously untracked full sibling, Richard D Cheesman (b. 16 Oct 1749, d. 1799), is also documented as Ann Ellis's son on WikiTree -- not currently in this tree at all.

Martha's own, independently-existing WikiTree profile (Taber-815) lists BOTH her parents as unknown (no link to Benjamin Taber/Eliza Bolton) and documents a real FIRST marriage: to Joseph Hedger, 1 Nov 1741, Philadelphia, 'at age 21' -- which independently corroborates HER birth year as ~1720 (consistent with this tree) and explains the 'Hedger' in her name (first husband, not a garbled compound surname). It names her actual documented children as Deborah (Hedger) Cheeseman and Maribeth (Hedger) Cheeseman (both b. 16 Mar 1738, Gloucester NJ) -- i.e. daughters by Joseph Hedger, NOT the five 'Cheesman' children this tree attaches to her. Notably, one of these Hedger daughters, Maribeth, went on to marry Thomas Cheesman (Peter's actual son by Ann Ellis) in 1771 -- Martha's real-life link to the Cheesman family may be as much through this daughter's marriage as through her own eventual (undated, but real -- see below) marriage to the widower Peter.

The 'Bet 1746 and 1748' marriage date to Peter looks misattached (possibly copied from one secondary source's 'c.1746' date for Ann Ellis's marriage to Peter, rather than Martha's own). A real land-deed abstract in the Adams manuscript records 'Peter (3) and Martha (3) (Hedger) Cheesman' jointly conveying 80 acres to George Sennor in 1781 -- i.e. Martha (as a widow, still carrying the Hedger surname) really was Peter's wife, but as a LATE-life marriage after Ann Ellis's 1759 death, not in 1746-48. Margaret Cheesman (b. Jan 1764, when Martha would be ~44) is the only one of this tree's five listed children chronologically compatible with Martha as an actual Cheesman-marriage mother, though no source names Margaret's mother directly (Peter's 1788 will bequeaths to 'Margaret (4) Pierce, wife of William Pierce' without stating parentage). Thomas John Cheeseman (no dates at all) is unattested in any external source found.

Net effect: none of William, Thomas, or Mary Ann should be treated as confirmed children of this Martha; Margaret is the best (unconfirmed) candidate; Thomas John is wholly unverified. Machine-owned relationships.children left unedited per repo convention (see the James McCue / Nancy Davis precedents in docs/research/direct-line-issues.md) -- this note supersedes the attachment. Full writeup: docs/research/ancestors/gen09-martha-taber-hedger-eliza-bolton-taber.md.

Separately, the parent-too-young flag on Martha's OWN 1720 birth (mother Eliza Bolton Taber, allegedly age 12) is addressed on Eliza's record, I182195863565.json -- short version: Martha's 1720 birth looks correct (independently corroborated by her 1741 first marriage, above), so the likelier error is the Eliza-Martha parent link itself, not either woman's birth year.
